Metadata.description: Free, open-source video meetings in your browser, on any device.

Landing.headline: Video meetings in your browser.
Landing.subline: Free and open source. Works on any device.
Landing.newHere: New here? <link>Create a free account</link> to host meetings.
Landing.featuresTitle: Everything you expect from a meeting app

anyDevice.title: Any device
anyDevice.body: Join from a link on Windows, Mac, iPhone, iPad or Android, in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox.

screenShare.title: Screen sharing with sound
screenShare.body: Share a tab, a window or your whole screen.

safety.title: Waiting room and passcodes
safety.body: Let people in when you're ready, and remove anyone.

desktopApp.title: Desktop app
desktopApp.body: For Mac and Windows: meeting links open in it, and you can mute from any app.

googleWorkspace.title: In Google Calendar and Gmail
googleWorkspace.body: Add a meeting to any event or email, right from Google’s own menus.

desktopAndGoogle.title: Desktop app and Google add-on
desktopAndGoogle.body: Apps for <desktop>Mac and Windows</desktop>, and meetings right in <google>Google Calendar and Gmail</google>.

installApp.title: Install it as an app
installApp.body: Add it to your computer or phone from the browser, and open it like any other app.

effects.title: Backgrounds and effects
effects.body: Blur your background, or swap in a picture or video, all on your own device.

openSource.title: Free and open source
openSource.body: MIT licensed, with no ads and no tracking. Run your own copy.

install.title: Install the app
install.intro: Open {appName} from your home screen, dock or taskbar, in a window of its own.

install.macSafari: In Safari’s menu bar, choose File › Add to Dock.

To count every email on the account right away, other apps’ included, add a full-access Resend key as RESEND_USAGE_API_KEY where {appName} is hosted, and redeploy.

vercel.title: Hosting (Vercel)
vercel.body: Vercel emails you itself as you near its free plan’s limits, so there’s nothing to count here.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.unavailable: Each meeting’s page has buttons to add it to Google Calendar, Outlook or any calendar app.

AddonSetup.title: {appName} in Google Calendar and Gmail
AddonSetup.addTitle: Add {appName} to Google Calendar and Gmail
AddonSetup.addBody: Choose {appName} meeting when you add video conferencing to an event, and start a meeting or put one in an email from a side panel in Calendar and Gmail. On a computer, in your browser.
AddonSetup.addHelp: {appName} makes you your own copy of its add-on, in your Google account. Google asks you to allow that first.
AddonSetup.inBrowser: Finish in your browser. It shows here once it’s done.
AddonSetup.createdTitle: One more step: install it in Google
AddonSetup.createdIntro: Your copy of the {appName} add-on is in your Google account. Install it once:
AddonSetup.stepInstall: In Apps Script, select Deploy, then Test deployments, then Install.
AddonSetup.stepUse: Open Google Calendar. The first time you use {appName} there, Google asks you to allow it and warns that it isn’t verified: that’s because it’s your own copy, not one from Google’s Marketplace. Select Advanced, then Go to {appName}, then Allow.
AddonSetup.whyInstall: Google installs an add-on that isn’t in its Marketplace only this way.
AddonSetup.connectedTitle: {appName} is in your Google Calendar and Gmail
AddonSetup.connectedBody: Choose {appName} meeting under Add video conferencing, or open {appName} from the side panel in Calendar and Gmail. It keeps itself up to date.
AddonSetup.updateBody: There’s a newer version of the add-on, and Google needs you to allow {appName} again to put it in your copy.
AddonSetup.removeLabel: Remove {appName} from Google Calendar and Gmail
AddonSetup.removeTitle: Remove {appName} from Google Calendar and Gmail?
AddonSetup.removeBody: {appName} stops answering your add-on. To take it out of Google too, uninstall it in Apps Script afterwards.
AddonSetup.removed: {appName} removed from Google Calendar and Gmail
AddonSetup.removedNotice: To take it out of Google too, open it in Apps Script and select Deploy, then Test deployments, then Uninstall. You can then delete the project from your Apps Script projects.
AddonSetup.turnOnApi: Turn it on in Google Cloud

readme.title: Your {appName} data
readme.account: `account.json`: your profile, the ways you sign in, your sign-in sessions and the settings kept with your account.
readme.hosting: `hosting.json`: whether you host full meetings, and your requests to.
readme.meetings: `meetings.json` and `meetings.csv`: the meetings you host, with their settings, invitees and co-hosts.
readme.previous: `previous.json` and `previous.csv`: the meetings you hosted or joined in the last {days} days, and who came. Email addresses appear only for you, and for the people you invited to meetings you host.
readme.notes: `notes.json` and the `notes` folder: the AI notes you can read, each with its transcript where it was saved with the notes, as data and as Markdown.
readme.notIn: What isn’t in it, and why
readme.media: Audio, video and screen sharing: they go between the people in a meeting, and {appName} never records them.
readme.chat: Chat messages and reactions: {appName} doesn’t store them.
readme.device: Settings kept on your device, such as your microphone, camera, time format and backgrounds: they stay in your browser.
readme.secrets: Your password and sign-in tokens: secrets that only sign you in.
readme.older: Meetings older than {days} days: they’re deleted by then, as the privacy policy says.
readme.times: Times in the JSON files are in UTC. The CSV files use {zone}.

readme.title: Your {appName} meeting history
readme.history: `history.csv`: one row for each meeting from the last {days} days that you hosted or joined: when it started, its title and host, your role, how long it lasted and how many people came.
readme.attendance: `attendance.csv`: who came to the meetings you hosted: their names, how they joined, when they first joined and last left, for how long, and how many times they joined. Email addresses appear only for you, and for the people you invited.
readme.notes: The `notes` folder: the AI notes you can read, each with its transcript where it was saved with the notes, as Markdown.
readme.account: Your account and the meetings you schedule: they’re in **Download your data**, under **Settings → Account**.

DesktopWelcome.title: Welcome to {appName}
DesktopWelcome.intro: Join a meeting with its ID or link, or sign in to start your own.
DesktopWelcome.noAccount: You don’t need an account to join.

DesktopCalendar.title: Connect Google Calendar
DesktopCalendar.connectedBody: You can close this tab and go back to {appName}.
DesktopCalendar.signIn: Sign in to {appName} in this browser to connect Google Calendar to your account.
DesktopCalendar.otherAccount: This browser is signed in as {email}, not the account you use in the {appName} app. Sign out here, then sign in with that account.
DesktopCalendar.unavailable: This copy of {appName} doesn’t offer Google Calendar.
